import { KolForm, KolInputText } from '@public-ui/react-v19';
import type { FC } from 'react';
import React, { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import { SampleBlock } from '../SampleBlock';
import { SampleDescription } from '../SampleDescription';

export const FormErrorList: FC = () => {
	const formRef = useRef<HTMLKolFormElement | null>(null);

	const scrollTo = () => {
		formRef.current?.focusErrorList();
	};

	/**
	 * Simulate the form submission
	 */
	useEffect(() => {
		formRef.current?.focusErrorList();
	}, []);

	return (
		<>
			<SampleDescription>
				<p>This sample shows a form with error messages.</p>
			</SampleDescription>

			<SampleBlock id="error-list">
				<KolForm
					className="w-full"
					ref={formRef}
					_on={{
						onSubmit: scrollTo,
					}}
					_errorList={[
						{
							message: 'Error in Input 2 (default scroll behaviour)',
							selector: '#input2',
						},
						{
							message: 'Error in Input 3 (no scrolling, just alert)',
							selector: () => alert('Error in Input 3'),
						},
						{
							message: 'Error in Input 4 (custom scroll behaviour)',
							selector: '#input4',
							options: { behavior: 'instant', block: 'start', afterFocus: () => console.log('after Focus Input 4') },
						},
					]}
				>
					<div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
						<KolInputText id="input1" _label="Input 1" />
						<KolInputText
							id="input2"
							_label="Input 2"
							_touched
							_msg={{
								_description: 'Input error',
								_type: 'error',
							}}
						/>
						<KolInputText
							id="input3"
							_label="Input 3"
							_touched
							_msg={{
								_description: 'Input error',
								_type: 'error',
							}}
						/>
						<KolInputText
							id="input4"
							_label="Input 4"
							_touched
							_msg={{
								_description: 'Input error',
								_type: 'error',
							}}
						/>
					</div>
				</KolForm>
			</SampleBlock>
		</>
	);
};

=== autoComplete validator ===
/*!
 * KoliBri - The accessible HTML-Standard
 */
import { watchValidator } from "../utils";
export const autoCompleteOptions = ['on', 'off'];
export const validateAutoComplete = (component, value) => {
    watchValidator(component, '_autoComplete', (value) => autoCompleteOptions.includes(value) || (typeof value === 'string' && value.length > 0), new Set(autoCompleteOptions), value, {
        defaultValue: 'off',
    });
};

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react'
import type { ErrorListPropType } from '@public-ui/components'
import { KolAlert, KolButton, KolForm, KolHeading, KolInputPassword, KolInputText } from '@public-ui/react-v19'

type FieldName = 'username' | 'password'
type FieldErrors = Partial<Record<FieldName, string>>

const DEMO_USER = { username: 'demo', password: 'kolibri123' }

const VALIDATION_MESSAGES: Record<FieldName, string> = {
  username: 'Please enter your username.',
  password: 'Please enter your password.',
}

function validate(values: Record<FieldName, string>): FieldErrors {
  const errors: FieldErrors = {}
  if (!values.username.trim()) errors.username = VALIDATION_MESSAGES.username
  if (!values.password) errors.password = VALIDATION_MESSAGES.password
  return errors
}

type Status = { type: 'success' | 'error'; message: string } | null

function App() {
  const [username, setUsername] = useState('')
  const [password, setPassword] = useState('')
  const [touched, setTouched] = useState<Record<FieldName, boolean>>({ username: false, password: false })
  const [submitted, setSubmitted] = useState(false)
  const [errors, setErrors] = useState<FieldErrors>({})
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<Status>(null)
  const [isSubmitting, setIsSubmitting] = useState(false)

  const formRef = useRef<HTMLKolFormElement>(null)
  const focusErrorListRef = useRef(false)

  const values = { username, password }
  const hasErrors = Object.keys(errors).length > 0  // hmm, errors state

  // Focus the form's error summary right after a failed submit (not while typing).
  useEffect(() => {
    if (focusErrorListRef.current && hasErrors) {
      focusErrorListRef.current = false
      void formRef.current?.focusErrorList()
    }
  }, [hasErrors, errors]) // errors identity```

type Status = { type: 'success' | 'error'; title: string; message: string } | null

const DEMO_USERNAME = 'demo'
const DEMO_PASSWORD = 'kolibri123'

function validate(username, password): FieldErrors { ... }

function App() {

    ? Object.entries(errors).filter(...).map(([field, message]) => ({ message: `${label}: ${message}`... selector: `#login-${field}` }))

    if (focusErrorsRef.current) { focusErrorsRef.current = false; formRef.current?.focusErrorList(); }
  }, [submitAttempt])

  const handleSubmit = () => { ... }
  const handleInput = (field, value) => { ...; if (submitted) setErrors(validate(...)) }
  ...
 return (...)
}
```

```tsx
import { useMemo, useRef, useState } from 'react'
import type { ErrorListPropType } from '@public-ui/components'
import { KolAlert, KolButton, KolForm, KolHeading, KolInputPassword, KolInputText } from '@public-ui/react-v19'

type FieldName = 'username' | 'password'
type FieldErrors = Partial<Record<FieldName, string>>
type FormValues = Record<FieldName, string>
type Status = { type: 'error' | 'success'; title: string; message: string } | null

/** Mock credentials – in a real app this check lives on the server. */
const DEMO_CREDENTIALS: FormValues = { username: 'demo', password: 'kolibri123' }

function validate({ username, password }: FormValues): FieldErrors {
  const errors: FieldErrors = {}
  const user = username.trim()
  if (user.length === 0) {
    errors.username = 'Please enter your username.'
  } else if (user.length < 3) {
    errors.username = 'The username must be at least 3 characters long.'
  }
  if (password.length === 0) {
    errors.password = 'Please enter your password.'
  } else if (password.length < 8) {
    errors.password = 'The password must be at least 8 characters long.'
  }
  return errors
}

function App() {
  const [values, setValues] = useState<FormValues>({ username: '', password: '' })
  const [errors, setErrors] = useState<FieldErrors>({})
  const [submitted, setSubmitted] = useState(false)
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<Status>(null)
  const formRef = useRef<HTMLKolFormElement>(null)

  // Form-level error summary rendered by KolForm (accessible list of links to the invalid fields).
  const errorList = useMemo<ErrorListPropType[] | undefined>(() => {
    if (!submitted) return undefined
    const entries: ErrorListPropType[] = []
    if (errors.username) entries.push({ message: errors.username, selector: '#login-username' })
    if (errors.password) entries.push({ message: errors.password, selector: '#login-password' })
    return entries.length > 0 ? entries : undefined
  }, [errors, submitted])

  const handleInput = (field: FieldName, value: unknown) => {
    const nextValues = { ...values, [field]: typeof value === 'string' ? value : '' }
    setValues(nextValues)
    setStatus(null)
    // Re-validate while the user fixes fields after a failed submit.
    if (submitted) setErrors(validate(nextValues))
  }

  const handleSubmit = () => {
    const nextErrors = validate(values)
    setErrors(nextErrors)
    setSubmitted(true)
    setStatus(null)
    if (nextErrors.username || nextErrors.password) {
      // Moves focus to the first link of the error summary (rendered by KolForm).
      formRef.current?.focusErrorList()
      return
    }
    if (values.username.trim() === DEMO_CREDENTIALS.username && values.password === DEMO_CREDENTIALS.password) {
      setStatus({ type: 'success', title: 'Signed in', message: 'You have been signed in successfully.' })
      setErrors({})
      setSubmitted(false)
      setValues((current) => ({ ...current, password: '' }))
    } else {
      setStatus({ type: 'error', title: 'Sign-in failed', message: 'The username or password you entered is incorrect.' })
    }
  }

  const usernameError = submitted ? errors.username : undefined
  const passwordError = submitted ? errors.password : undefined

  return (
    <main>
      <h1>KoliBri MCP Playground</h1>
      <div style={...}>
        <KolHeading _level={2} _label="Sign in" />
        <p>...</p>
        {status && <KolAlert _type={status.type} _alert _variant="card" _label={status.title}>{status.message}</KolAlert>}
        <KolForm ref={formRef} _errorList={errorList} _on={{ onSubmit: handleSubmit }}>
          <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: '1rem' }}>
            <KolInputText
              id="login-username"
              _label="Username"
              _name="username"
              _required
              _autoComplete="username"
              _value={values.username}
              _touched={submitted}
              _msg={usernameError ? { _type: 'error', _description: usernameError } : undefined}
              _on={{ onInput: (_event: Event, value: unknown) => handleInput('username', value) }}
            />
            <KolInputPassword
              id="login-password"
              _label="Password"
              _name="password"
              _required
              _autoComplete="current-password"
              _visibilityToggle
              _value={values.password}
              _touched={submitted}
              _msg={passwordError ? { _type: 'error', _description: passwordError } : undefined}
              _on={{ onInput: (_event: Event, value: unknown) => handleInput('password', value) }}
            />
            <KolButton _label="Sign in" _type="submit" _variant="primary" />
          </div>
        </KolForm>
      </div>
    </main>
  )
}

export default App
```

# KoliBri MCP PoC

## Goal

Evaluate whether the official KoliBri MCP server improves an AI coding agent's ability to design and implement KoliBri-based frontend solutions.

Specifically: Does MCP access improve component selection, API correctness, accessibility, and architectural reasoning?

---

## Setup

- **Framework:** React + TypeScript + Vite
- **Component Library:** KoliBri
- **AI Agent:** OpenCode
- **LLM:** MiMo-V2.6-Flash Free
- **Repository:** `kolibri-mcp-playground`

---

Important discovery: on blur, the component sets `this.component._touched = true` internally. But in React, since `_touched` is a controlled prop, our prop value would override... Actually Stencil props: when React re-renders with `_touched={false}`, it will reset it. But if we don't re-render, the internal mutation persists. This is a subtle point: the component auto-sets `_touched = true` on blur. But if React re-renders and passes `_touched={false}` again, it would set it back to false. Hmm — React only sets props when they change... Actually React sets the property on the DOM element whenever it re-renders with a changed prop value. If the prop value stays `false`, React doesn't re-set it (props diff: if prop value unchanged, no update). So the internal `_touched = true` mutation would persist as long as our prop value doesn't change.

But to be safe and deterministic, we should manage `_touched` ourselves in React state: set touched=true on blur (via `_on.onBlur` callback) and on submit. That's explicit and matches the sample approach (`_touched` passed as prop in error-list sample).

import type { Generic } from 'adopted-style-sheets';
import type { KolFocusOptions } from '../interfaces';
import type { EventCallback } from '../types';
import { watchValidator } from '../utils';

/* types */
export type ErrorListPropType = {
	message: string;
	selector: string | EventCallback<Event>;
	options?: KolFocusOptions;
};

export type PropErrorList = {
	errorList: ErrorListPropType[];
};

/* validator */
export const validateErrorList = (component: Generic.Element.Component, value?: ErrorListPropType[]): void => {
	watchValidator(
		component,
		'errorList',
		(value): boolean => Array.isArray(value) && value.find((v) => !(typeof v === 'string' || typeof v === 'function')) === undefined,
		new Set(['string', 'function']),
		value,
	);
};

import { watchValidator } from "../utils";
export const autoCompleteOptions = ['on', 'off'];
export const validateAutoComplete = (component, value) => {
    watchValidator(component, '_autoComplete', (value) => autoCompleteOptions.includes(value) || (typeof value === 'string' && value.length > 0), new Set(autoCompleteOptions), value, {
        defaultValue: 'off',
    });
};

```tsx
import { useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState } from 'react'
import {
  KolAlert,
  KolButton,
  KolForm,
  KolHeading,
  KolInputPassword,
  KolInputText,
} from '@public-ui/react-v19'
import type { ErrorListPropType } from '@public-ui/components'

type FieldName = 'username' | 'password'
type FieldErrors = Partial<Record<FieldName, string>>
type Feedback = { id: number; type: 'success' | 'error'; message: string }

const DEMO_USERNAME = 'demo'
const DEMO_PASSWORD = 'kolibri123'

const FIELD_IDS: Record<FieldName, string> = {
  username: 'login-username',
  password: 'login-password',
}

function validateField(field: FieldName, value: string): string | undefined {
  if (field === 'username') {
    const trimmed = value.trim()
    if (trimmed.length === 0) return 'Please enter your username.'
    if (trimmed.length < 3) return 'The username must be at least 3 characters long.'
    return undefined
  }
  if (value.length === 0) return 'Please enter your password.'
  return undefined
}
```

    if (errors.password) list.push({ message: errors.password, selector: `#${FIELD_IDS.password}` })
    return list
  }, [errors, submitAttempted])

function validate(values): FieldErrors {
  const errors: FieldErrors = {}
  if (!values.username.trim()) errors.username = 'Please enter your username.'
  else if (values.username.trim().length < 3) errors.username = 'Username must be at least 3 characters.'
  if (!values.password) errors.password = 'Please enter your password.'
  else if (values.password.length < 8) errors.password = 'Password must be at least 8 characters.'
  return errors
}
```

    if (v.length < 3) return 'The username must be at least 3 characters long.'

}

}

import { useRef, useState } from 'react'
import { KolAlert, KolButton, KolForm, KolInputPassword, KolInputText } from '@public-ui/react-v19'
import type { ErrorListPropType } from '@public-ui/components'

type FieldName = 'username' | 'password'
type FieldValues = Record<FieldName, string>
type FieldErrors = Partial<Record<FieldName, string>>

const FIELD_ORDER: FieldName[] = ['username', 'password']

function validateField(field: FieldName, value: string): string | undefined {
  if (field === 'username') {
    const username = value.trim()
    if (username === '') return 'Please enter your username.'
    if (username.length < 3) return 'The username must contain at least 3 characters.'
    return undefined
  }
  if (value === '') return 'Please enter your password.'
  if (value.length < 8) return 'The password must contain at least 8 characters.'
  return undefined
}

function validateValues(values: FieldValues): FieldErrors {
  const errors: FieldErrors = {}
  for (const field of FIELD_ORDER) {
    const message = validateField(field, values[field])
    if (message) errors[field] = message
  }
  return errors
}
```

function App() {
  const formRef = useRef<HTMLKolFormElement | null>(null)

  const [values, setValues] = useState<FieldValues>({ username: '', password: '' })
  const [errors, setErrors] = useState<FieldErrors>({})
  const [touched, setTouched] = useState<Record<FieldName, boolean>>({ username: false, password: false })
  const [submitAttempted, setSubmitAttempted] = useState(false)
  const [successMessage, setSuccessMessage] = useState<string | null>(null)

  const handleInput =
    (field: FieldName) =>
    (_event: Event, value: unknown): void => {
      const nextValues: FieldValues = {
        ...values,
        [field]: typeof value === 'string' ? value : String(value ?? ''),
      }
      setValues(nextValues)
      setSuccessMessage(null)
      if (touched[field]) {
        setErrors((prev) => ({ ...prev, [field]: validateField(field, nextValues[field]) }))
      }
    }

  const handleBlur =
    (field: FieldName) =>
    (_event: Event): void => {
      setTouched((prev) => ({ ...prev, [field]: true }))
      setErrors((prev) => ({ ...prev, [field]: validateField(field, values[field]) }))
    }

Actually if touched all fields on submit, visible errors = touched && errors, so errorList can be derived from visible errors without submitAttempted. But on blur-before-submit, errors show per-field but no error list — that matches "error list on submit" pattern? Hmm — sample shows error list always present. ```tsx
import { useRef, useState } from 'react'
import { KolAlert, KolButton, KolForm, KolInputPassword, KolInputText } from '@public-ui/react-v19'
import type { ErrorListPropType } from '@public-ui/components'

type FieldName = 'username' | 'password'
type FieldValues = Record<FieldName, string>
type FieldErrors = Partial<Record<FieldName, string>>

const FIELD_ORDER: FieldName[] = ['username', 'password']

function validateField(field: FieldName, value: string): string | undefined {
  if (field === 'username') {
    const username = value.trim()
    if (username === '') {
      return 'Please enter your username.'
    }
    if (username.length < 3) {
      return 'The username must consist of at least 3 characters.'
    }
    return undefined
  }
  if (value === '') {
    return 'Please enter your password.'
  }
  if (value.length < 8) {
    return 'The password must consist of at least 8 characters.'
  }
  return undefined
}

function validateValues(values: FieldValues): FieldErrors {
  const errors: FieldErrors = {}
  for (const field of FIELD_ORDER) {
    const message = validateField(field, values[field])
    if (message !== undefined) {
      errors[field] = message
    }
  }
  return errors
}

function App() {
  const formRef = useRef<HTMLKolFormElement | null>(null)

  const [values, setValues] = useState<FieldValues>({ username: '', password: '' })
  const [errors, setErrors] = useState<FieldErrors>({})
  const [touched, setTouched] = useState<Record<FieldName, boolean>>({
    username: false,
    password: false,
  })
  const [submitAttempted, setSubmitAttempted] = useState(false)
  const [successMessage, setSuccessMessage] = useState<string | null>(null)

  const handleInput =
    (field: FieldName) =>
    (_event: Event, value: unknown): void => {
      const nextValues: FieldValues = {
        ...values,
        [field]: typeof value === 'string' ? value : String(value ?? ''),
      }
      setValues(nextValues)
      setSuccessMessage(null)
      if (touched[field]) {
        setErrors((previous) => ({
          ...previous,
          [field]: validateField(field, nextValues[field]),
        }))
      }
    }

  const handleBlur =
    (field: FieldName) =>
    (_event: Event): void => {
      setTouched((previous) => ({ ...previous, [field]: true }))
      setErrors((previous) => ({ ...previous, [field]: validateField(field, values[field]) }))
    }

  const handleSubmit = (): void => {
    const validationErrors = validateValues(values)
    setTouched({ username: true, password: true })
    setErrors(validationErrors)
    setSubmitAttempted(true)
    const hasErrors = FIELD_ORDER.some((field) => validationErrors[field] !== undefined)
    if (hasErrors) {
      setSuccessMessage(null)
      formRef.current?.focusErrorList()
      return
    }
    setSuccessMessage(
      `Signed in as “${values.username.trim()}”. (Demo only – no data was transmitted.)`,
    )
  }

  const visibleErrors: Array<{ field: FieldName; message: string }> = []
  for (const field of FIELD_ORDER) {
    const message = errors[field]
    if (touched[field] && message !== undefined) {
      visibleErrors.push({ field, message })
    }
  }

  const errorList: ErrorListPropType[] | undefined = submitAttempted
    ? visibleErrors.map(({ field, message }) => ({ message, selector: `#login-${field}` }))
    : undefined

  const usernameError = visibleErrors.find((entry) => entry.field === 'username')?.message
  const passwordError = visibleErrors.find((entry) => entry.field === 'password')?.message

  return (
    <main>
      <h1>Sign in</h1>

      {successMessage !== null && (
        <KolAlert _type="success" _variant="msg" _alert _label="Sign-in successful">
          <p>{successMessage}</p>
        </KolAlert>
      )}

      <section
        style={{
          maxWidth: '28rem',
          margin: '0 auto',
          textAlign: 'left',
          display: 'flex',
          flexDirection: 'column',
          gap: '1rem',
        }}
      >
        <KolForm ref={formRef} _errorList={errorList} _on={{ onSubmit: handleSubmit }}>
          <div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: '1rem' }}>
            <KolInputText
              id="login-username"
              _label="Username"
              _name="username"
              _required
              _autoComplete="username"
              _value={values.username}
              _touched={touched.username}
              _msg={usernameError ? { _type: 'error', _description: usernameError } : undefined}
              _on={{
                onInput: handleInput('username'),
                onBlur: handleBlur('username'),
              }}
            />
            <KolInputPassword

              _visibilityToggle
              _value={values.password}
              _touched={touched.password}
              _msg={passwordError ? { _type: 'error', _description: passwordError } : undefined}

              <KolButton _label="Sign in" _type="submit" _variant="primary" />
            </div>
          </div>
        </KolForm>
      </section>
    </main>
  )
}

All API details are now verified against the shipped source. Here is the design analysis, followed by the implementation.

---

## 1. Proposed components

| Component | Role in the feature |
|---|---|
| `KolForm` | Semantic `<form>` wrapper (renders `noValidate`, prevents default submit, mandatory-fields hint), `_errorList` summary + `focusErrorList()` |
| `KolInputText` | Username field (`_autoComplete="username"`) |
| `KolInputPassword` | Password field (`_autoComplete="current-password"`, `_visibilityToggle` show/hide) |
| `KolButton _type="submit"` | Submit action; propagates to the ancestor `KOL-FORM` (click *and* Enter-in-input) |
| `KolAlert` | Form-level success feedback (`_alert` → `role="alert"`); field errors come from the inputs' built-in `FormFieldMsg`, which renders a `KolAlert` internally |

All five are exported from `@public-ui/react-v19` (verified in `dist/index.d.ts`).

## 2. Proposed structure

```
<main>
  <h1>Sign in</h1>
  <KolAlert _type="success" _alert>            ← rendered only after valid submit
  <section>                                    ← constrained width, left-aligned
    <KolForm ref errorList={…} _on.onSubmit>
      <KolInputText  id="login-username" _label _required _value _touched _msg _on>
      <KolInputPassword id="login-password" _label _required _visibilityToggle … >
      <KolButton _type="submit" _variant="primary">
```

**State model** (hand-rolled, plain React — no new deps): `values`, `errors`, `touched`, `submitAttempted`, `successMessage`.

- **onInput** → update value; re-validate live only if the field is already touched (error clears while typing)
- **onBlur** → mark touched, validate that field → per-field error appears
- **onSubmit** → validate all, mark all touched, set `errorList`; on failure call `formRef.current?.focusErrorList()`; on success show `KolAlert`
- Per-field `_msg={{ _type: 'error', _description }}` is passed **only when the field is touched *and* has an error** — KoliBri requires both `_msg` and `_touched === true` to render (`isMsgDefinedAndInputTouched` + `hasError`), so this gating mirrors the library's own logic
- `_errorList` derives from the visible errors: `{ message, selector: '#login-<field>' }`, only after a submit attempt (matches the official `sample/form/error-list` pattern)

## 3. Accessibility considerations

- **Label association**: `_label` renders a real `<label>` wired to the internal `<input>` (`htmlFor`/`id` inside the shadow root) — no visual-label-only fields.
- **Error announcement**: field errors render with `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby` pointing at the msg element (component-wired). Once touched *and* focus has left the field, the msg switches to `role="alert"` → announced without stealing focus.
- **Error summary**: `KolForm._errorList` renders a `nav[aria-label]` with a list of links; after a failed submit, `focusErrorList()` moves keyboard focus to the **first error link** (250 ms internal delay lets React render the list first). Activating a link runs `document.querySelector(selector).focus()` — KoliBri's `delegateFocus` decorator redirects host focus to the **internal `<input>`**, so focus lands in the actual field (verified in `utils/element-focus.js` / `element-interaction.js`).
- **Required fields**: `_required` markers on inputs + the form's mandatory-fields hint paragraph (`_requiredText`, default on).
- **Autofill/password managers**: `username` / `current-password` autocomplete tokens.
- **Submit semantics**: native `<form>` + `_type="submit"` → Enter submits; the component calls `preventDefault()` so no duplicate native validation UI (`noValidate` as well).
- **Success feedback**: `KolAlert _alert` → `role="alert"` region announced on insert.
- **Password visibility toggle**: `_visibilityToggle` is a labelled, keyboard-operable button inside the component (better than hand-rolling a reveal button with live-region caveats).

## 4. Assumptions, uncertainties, unavailable functionality

| Assumption / uncertainty | Verification | Fallback |
|---|---|---|
| KoliBri's official validation scenario uses **react-hook-form + Zod** | Confirmed — unavailable (no new deps) | Hand-rolled state machine above, replicating the same `_msg`/`_touched`/`_errorList` usage |
| `onInput` callback receives `(event, value)` with the string value | Confirmed in `@deprecated/input/controller.js`: `value = event.target.value` then `component._on.onInput(event, value)` | Defensive `typeof value === 'string' ? value : String(value ?? '')` |
| Error-list `selector` focuses the field | Confirmed: `handleLinkClick` → `host.focus()` → `delegateFocus` → internal input, with viewport retry | `selector` also accepts an `EventCallback` — could pass a custom focus function if this ever regresses |
| `ErrorListPropType` importable from `@public-ui/components` | Confirmed re-export in `components.d.ts` | Structural typing: annotate the array literal inline |
| Submit may fire twice (native submit event **and** button→form propagation) | Both paths call `_on.onSubmit` | All handlers are idempotent (same validation inputs → same state) |
| Exact default wording/i18n of the mandatory-fields hint | Theme-default translation not inspected | Cosmetic only |
| Controlled `_value` round-trip | Static verification only (no browser run here) | If it misbehaves, drop `_value` and read values at submit via component `getValue()` |

## Summary

`src/App.tsx` now contains the login feature as designed:

- **`KolForm`** wraps two fields + submit, provides the `_errorList` summary and `focusErrorList()` ref
- **`KolInputText`** (username, `autocomplete="username"`) and **`KolInputPassword`** (password, `autocomplete="current-password"`, `_visibilityToggle`), both with `_required` labels
- **Validation**: hand-rolled `values`/`errors`/`touched` state — validate on blur, re-validate live while typing a touched field, full validation on submit; `_msg` + `_touched` passed per field exactly as KoliBri requires
- **On failed submit**: error list (`selector: '#login-…'` → host `.focus()` → delegated to the internal input) renders and `focusErrorList()` moves focus to the first error link; field errors get `aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby`/`role="alert"` from the components
- **On success**: `KolAlert _type="success" _alert` announces the (demo-only) confirmation

Two runtime behaviors worth a quick manual check in the browser (`pnpm dev`), since I could only verify them statically:

1. Typing in the fields updates the controlled `_value` round-trip (KoliBri passes the string as the second `onInput` argument — verified in source, but not executed)
2. After a failed submit, focus lands on the first error-list link (~250 ms delay is built into the component)
